newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Resolution to Leopardstown betting dispute agreed.
newsitem.headline: Resolution to Leopardstown betting dispute agreed.

text.p: The Irish Horseracing Authority (IHA) and the Irish National Bookmakers Association (INBA) on Thursday agreed on a resolution to the dispute in relation to the on-course betting shop at Leopardstown racecourse.

In a joint statement the bodies said an independent consultant would be appointed immediately to evaluate the results of the trial carried out on the SP (starting-price) shop at Leopardstown in 1996 on agreed terms of reference.
Both sides agree to be bound by the findings and recommendations of the consultant and the cost of the consultancy will be borne by both, the statement said.
The statement said no bets on the home meeting will be taken in the SP shop until the consultant reports.

Both sides agreed that a comprehensive study should be carried out on on-course betting in relation to horseracing while other issues relating to the levy system and matters affecting the ring had been agreed for implementation, the statement said.
On-course bookmakers boycotted the Leopardstown race meeting of January 11 in order to highlight their disapproval of the on-course betting shop at the racecourse.
